questions.q: A five–men (1)/ enquiry committee was appointed (2)/ to look into the matter. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.s: Replace 'five–men' with 'five–man'. In compound adjectives with numbers, the noun remains singular:

questions.q: These stray cattle is roaming around the town.CPO- 14/3/2019 S3
questions.s:
The noun “cattle” is plural in meaning, though it does not take “-s.”
Therefore, it must be used with a plural verb.
Correct Sentence: These stray cattle are roaming around the town.

questions.q: Lalitha will go / to sister's house / in Mumbai / this summer. (CGL 18/8/2021 S1)
questions.s:
"sister's house" needs a possessive determiner (her/his/my/their) to show whose sister it is
Without "her," the sentence is grammatically incomplete and unclear.
Correct sentence: "Lalitha will go to her sister's house in Mumbai this summer.”

questions.q: His mean / are very limited / yet he does not curtail / his expenditure and spends lavishly.
questions.s:
Explanation:- Use ‘means’ in place of ‘mean’.

'Income/resources' wale meaning me means word ka hi use hota hai iske sath verb plural aati hai.

questions.q: The Sharma's/ have been living here/ for about a decade / No error.
o: have been living here
for about a decade
questions.s:
The correct answer is: the Sharma's

  • "The Sharma's" is incorrect because the apostrophe + "s" is used to show possession. For a family name, we use the plural form without an apostrophe: "The Sharmas" (to refer to all members of the Sharma family).

Corrected Sentence: The Sharmas have been living here for about a decade.

questions.q: He honed his culinary talents by attending cooking classes.
questions.s:
Here the use of talents is not correct. Skills should come in place of talents because we use “skill” when we acquire it by learning while “talent” when it comes naturally.

Therefore, the correct sentence would be: “He honed his culinary skills by attending cooking classes.”

questions.q: He told me that it was his friend’s Meera’s house.
questions.s:
Change ‘friend’s’ into friend. Double apostrophes cannot be used in a sentence.

So the correct sentence is He told me that it was his friend Meera’s house.

questions.q: Envy consumes him when he notices his girlfriend laughing with another man.
questions.s:
"Jealousy" typically refers to the fear of losing something one already possesses, such as a relationship or possession, to another person. On the other hand, "envy" typically refers to the desire for something possessed by someone else. So, here jealousy should come in place of envy

Therefore, the correct sentence would be: “Jealousy consumes him when he notices his girlfriend laughing with another man.”

questions.q: The first inning (1)/ of the match (2)/ was very sensational. (3)/ No error. (4)
questions.s: Replace 'inning' with 'innings'. In cricket (and British English), the word is "innings" for both singular and plural. "The first innings was very sensational."

questions.q: There was / no money in the bank / in Dhananjay’s / and Mritunjay’s joint account.
questions.s:
Explanation:- Use ‘Dhananjay’ in place of ‘Dhananjay’s’.

Permission (uncountable) :- the action of officially allowing someone to do a particular thing.

Permissions (plural noun) official written statement allowing someone to do something.

questions.q: I had a hard time paying the driver as I had only hundreds rupee note.
o: only hundreds rupee note
I had a hard time
questions.s:
Replace “hundreds rupee note” with “a hundred-rupee note” or “hundred-rupee notes.”
When numbers are used as compound adjectives before a noun, the first noun remains singular (e.g., a five-star hotel, a hundred-rupee note).

questions.q: Shall / we go / for walking / in the park?
questions.s:
Explanation:- (d) use ‘a walk’ instead of ‘walking’ kyunki 'go for a walk/ride/drive/run/swim' ek fixed phrase hota hai.

Note :- Jahan noun 'possible' hota hai wahan jabardasti gerund nahi lagate hain.

questions.q: I saw (1)/ two deers (2)/ in the woods. (3)/ No error (4).
questions.s: The plural of deer remains deer, not deers. So, the correct sentence is I saw two deer in the woods.

questions.q: Identify the type of noun underlined: "The Ganga is a sacred river in India."
questions.s: "Ganga" is a proper noun because it is the specific name of a particular river and is capitalized. Proper nouns refer to specific names of people, places, or things. "Ganga" is not abstract (quality/idea), material (substance), or collective (group).

questions.q: The beautiful (1)/ surrounding of the place (2)/ enchanted me. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.s: Replace 'surrounding' with 'surroundings'. The word "surroundings" (meaning the environment/area around) is always plural.

questions.q: My father gave me (1)/ a pair of binocular (2)/ on my birthday. (3)/ No error. (4)
questions.s: Replace 'binocular' with 'binoculars'. The word is always plural: "a pair of binoculars."

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’.
o: a lot of homework
questions.s:
Answer: a lot of homework
Solution:

  • The underlined phrase is “a lot of homeworks”, which is incorrect because “homework” is an uncountable noun and does not take a plural form.

  • The correct expression is: “a lot of homework” ✅

  • Option meanings:

  • A lots of homework – ❌ grammatically incorrect (double plural)

  • No substitution – ❌ incorrect as "homeworks" is wrong

  • Much homework – grammatically correct but less natural in spoken English

  • A lot of homework – ✅ correct and natural usage for uncountable noun "homework"

questions.q: The balance in his saving / account is not enough for him to / avail himself of these facilities.
o: account is not enough for him to
questions.s:
Explanation:- Use ‘savings’ in place of ‘saving’.

'Savings' and 'earnings' humesha plural me hi likhe jaate hain.

questions.q: All our / furnitures were / spoiled in the recent / rains and floods. CHSL 4/8/2021 S2
o: spoiled in the recent
questions.s: "Furniture" is an uncountable noun and has no plural form. The correct form would be "furniture was".

questions.q: Ram is a ( hardworking men). (Phase - X (GRAD. LEVEL)
questions.s: The article "a" requires a singular noun. "Men" is plural, so "man" should be used.

questions.q: Scholars have / studied the lives of / present-day farmer's / who practice agriculture. (MTS 22/07/2022 S2)
o: studied the lives of
questions.s: The apostrophe in farmer's shows possession (belonging), but here it is meant to be plural referring to many farmers. So, it should be present-day farmers, not farmer’s. Apostrophe is unnecessary unless showing ownership (e.g., farmer’s field).

questions.q: In mathematics, locuses are sets of points that satisfy a particular condition.
o: are sets of points that
questions.s:
"Loci" is the plural form of "locus." So, “Loci” should be come in place of Locuses.

Therefore, the sentence should read: "In mathematics, loci are sets of points that satisfy a particular condition."

questions.s: Gold” refers to a substance or material from which things are made (like jewelry or coins).
